Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:1: Now that in the preceding chapters we have discussed the holiness of all the organs of the head, let us come to explain the matter of the holiness of the covenant [brit], regarding marital union — how its holiness is to be achieved. We shall explain two aspects of this: first, the existence of the holiness of union itself, and second, the timing of union. We shall not trouble ourselves to copy the words of our Sages of blessed memory, since the sage Rabbi Yitzchak Aboab has already copied them in his book Menorat HaMaor, and we rely on the reader to see his words there, since they are needed for the practical knowledge of many details. Rather, in this chapter we shall copy only the words of Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai, peace be upon him, which are scattered here and there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:2: Our holy Torah has commanded us (Leviticus 11:44), "and you shall sanctify yourselves and you shall be holy," and our Sages of blessed memory explained that this holiness was said regarding the holiness of marital relations. These are their words, in the chapter "Knowledge of Impurity" (Shevuot 18b): Rabbi Binyamin ben Yefet said, whoever sanctifies himself at the time of marital relations will have male children, as it is written, "and you shall sanctify yourselves and you shall be holy," and adjacent to it, "a woman who conceives" (ibid. 12:2). Thus far their words. And likewise the words of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in portion Tazria (49a) agree with this, as we shall copy below regarding the timing of union.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:3: And so they explained in the Zohar (portion Kedoshim, 81a) that this too is what is meant by (Leviticus 19:2), "you shall be holy." These are his words: come and see, at the time a person is found in union, male and female, and intends to sanctify properly, then he is whole and is called "one" without blemish. Therefore a person must gladden his wife at that time, to invite her with a single desire together with him, and both should intend as one for that matter; and when both are found as one, then all is one, in soul and in body — in soul, to cleave one to the other with a single desire, and in body, as we have learned that an unmarried man is like one who is divided; and when male and female join, then they become one body, and they are found to be one soul and one body, and are called one person. Then the Holy One, blessed be He, rests upon that "one," and brings forth a spirit of holiness in that "one," and these are called children of the Holy One, blessed be He, as has been said. Therefore, "you shall be holy, for I, the LORD, am holy." Fortunate is Israel, who has established this matter [holiness] on none but Him alone, as it is written, "for I, the LORD, am holy" — to cleave to Him and not to another; and therefore, "you shall be holy, for I, the LORD your God, am holy." Thus far his words. It is thus explained from the end of this statement that the commandment "you shall be holy" concerns the holiness of union, and we shall explain further below what he has clarified regarding the holiness of union.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:4: Know that according to how a person sanctifies himself at that time, so he draws down to his heart a holy soul. This is explained in the Zohar (portion Shemot, 11b), these are his words: "and a man of the house of Levi went" (Exodus 2:1) — this is Gabriel, as it is said (Daniel 9:21), "and the man Gabriel whom I had seen in the vision before" etc. "Of the house of Levi" — this is the Community of Israel, which comes from the side of the left. "And he took a daughter of Levi" — this is the soul, for we have learned that when the body of a righteous person is born into this world, the Holy One, blessed be He, calls Gabriel, and takes that soul of the righteous one that is in the Garden and brings it down into this body of the righteous one born into this world, and he [Gabriel] is appointed over it and guards it. And should you say, is not the angel appointed over the spirits of the righteous named "Laylah" [Night], and you say it is Gabriel? — indeed it is so, since he comes from the side of the left, and everyone who comes from the side of the left is called thus. "And a man went" — this is Amram; "and he took a daughter of Levi" — this is Yocheved; and a heavenly voice descended and told him to marry her, since the time of Israel's redemption was drawing near, through the son who would be born to them, and the Holy One, blessed be He, assisted him — for we have learned that the Shechinah rested upon their bed, and their desire was in a single attachment with the Shechinah; and therefore the Shechinah did not depart from that son they bore, to be established, as it is written, "and you shall sanctify yourselves and you shall be holy" — a person sanctifies himself below, [and] the Holy One, blessed be He, sanctifies him above; just as their desire was in attachment to the Shechinah, so did the Shechinah attach itself to that very deed which they performed.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:5: Rabbi Yitzchak said: fortunate are the righteous whose desire is continually in attachment to the Holy One, blessed be He, for just as they continually attach themselves to Him, so too He attaches Himself to them and never abandons them. Woe to the wicked, whose desire and attachment distance themselves from Him — and it is not enough that they distance themselves from Him, but they attach themselves to the other side. Come and see: Amram, who attached himself to the Holy One, blessed be He, Moses issued from him. Thus far his words, as relevant to our purpose.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:6: Further, in the Zohar (portion Chayei Sarah, end of 130), these are his words: in like manner, every person in the world is composed of above and below, and all those who know how to sanctify themselves in this world properly — when they beget a son, a spirit of holiness is drawn upon it from the place from which all holy things issue, and these are called sons of the Holy One, blessed be He, because the body was made in holiness properly; likewise they are given a spirit from the supernal, holy place as is fitting, and this has been said. Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:7: Know that the existence of the holiness of union depends on a person knowing how to attach himself to the Holy One, blessed be He, and knowing how to unite the attributes in spiritual reality. For just as he knows how to strip physicality from things above, so he must know how to strip his thought from thinking about that act as an indulgence in the vanity of this world — for one whose intent in that act is for pleasure resembles an animal, as we wrote in this gate, chapter 4, regarding one who sanctifies himself below; and as we elaborated in the Gate of Love, chapter 10, in explaining the statement of Rashbi, peace be upon him. Therefore he said in this statement before us, "fortunate are the righteous whose desire is continually in attachment to the Holy One, blessed be He" — for the righteous, whose intent is always to be attached to Him, do not separate from Him even at that time; this is what is meant by "continually."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:8: The parable for this is the existence of the intent of eating that we wrote above in the preceding chapters — that although the bodily organs benefit from that eating, the thought is attached above, thinking of the spirituality of the eating; likewise in this matter is the existence of union.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:9: What the reader needs to know, how to strip himself entirely in union from the aspect of the evil inclination, is that he should think that the aspect of that organ is an organ like the other 248 organs of a person, some revealed, some hidden. Before the sin of Adam it is said (Genesis 2:25), "and the two of them were naked, the man and his wife, and they were not ashamed," and our Sages of blessed memory said in Vayikra Rabbah, at the beginning of portion Acharei Mot, Rabbi Levi in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya: the heel of Adam dimmed the orb of the sun, how much more so the radiance of his face; see there. And likewise it says in Tikkunim (10b): at first, garments of light, whose heel dimmed the orb of the sun, etc. Certainly his other organs too were, in this respect, more luminous, and the evil inclination did not rule over them; therefore "they were not ashamed." And what caused them shame? From the side of nakedness [ervah], which is the evil inclination that blemished them; but before, this organ was to them like a hand or foot — since the mitzvah of the union of a man and his wife is through this organ, it is like the laying of tefillin on the left hand and the head-tefillin on the brain, and just as these have no evil inclination, so too in that organ which fulfills the mitzvah of procreation with which Adam was commanded before the sin, all is one, and it is not fitting that there be an evil inclination in it. And what caused the evil inclination to be in it, and that it needed covering and was called "ervah"? The sin that occurred was the blemish, which is [the letters of] "ra" [evil] and "vav-heh" [drawn out through] his foreskin, and it became materialized and ruled over this organ.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:10: The main task of the righteous in this world is to rectify the blemish of Adam, for Adam included all the souls, and all sinned, and all need to be rectified. Now, the righteous who attach themselves to the Holy One, blessed be He, in the secret of their thought, rectify the secret of the supernal thought in which Adam's blemish occurred, as explained in Tikkunim (99b), that Adam sinned in thought and Eve in deed; see there, and also see 113a. And through the rectification of thought, which is the letter yod, the lower yod that is in the covenant is necessarily rectified as well.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:11: The reason for this is that when a person's thought turns to worldly matters in lustfulness and his heart follows after material things, the yod of the covenant becomes blemished, for immediately his "bow" becomes aroused, as it is written (Leviticus 19:4), "do not turn to idols and become defiled by them," as explained in portion Kedoshim (84a), that one who gazes at a woman and fantasizes about her by day is made impure by night, and his impurity is through the sign of the covenant, which is the yod that includes within it all the organs of the body.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:12: This was the sin of Adam's blemish, that he gave the evil inclination dominion over his whole body, and uprooted himself from the spirituality of the supernal holiness that is free of the evil inclination, and clothed himself in the physicality of the world and its powers and in lustfulness and other kelipot like it — the kelipah of lustfulness being the one that includes all. Therefore our Sages of blessed memory said that the Holy One, blessed be He, is jealous of lustfulness more than all other transgressions — the reason being that one uproots himself, his organs, and his soul entirely from all holiness and clothes himself completely in the evil inclination, which is not so with other transgressions — except for the matter of eating, which is a transgression that likewise entirely defiles the soul, since that impurity becomes an actual part of an organ in his body; and lustfulness is equal to it, for the term "eating" is also used of it, as it is said (Proverbs 30:20), "she eats and wipes her mouth."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:13: When a person attaches himself continually to the Holy One, blessed be He, and does not think of temporal, perishable material matters, and desires only to attach himself to the essential life-force that gives life to all, which is the secret of love explained in the Gate of Love — certainly then his "bow" is not aroused, and he does not come to impurity in any way; and then his union will be holy and will not be drawn to the side of the evil inclination at all, but his matter will be as Adam was before his sin, purely for the fulfillment of a mitzvah — for in a mitzvah one resembles one's Maker, as Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained in the statement we copied from portion Kedoshim, that just as He, blessed be He, is holy, so He commanded us to be holy, as it says at the end of the statement, "fortunate is Israel who has established this matter on none but Him alone, as it is written (Leviticus 19:2), 'for I, the LORD, am holy'" etc. — meaning that just as the existence of union, that is "ANI [I] HaShem [the LORD]," is called holy, being free of the evil inclination, so we must resemble Him, since the essence of holiness pertains to our spiritual souls that are emanated from Him, blessed be He.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:14: And if, God forbid, one thinks in this act of vain pleasure, he clothes his spiritual soul in the evil inclination, the opposite of the divine intent, and for this David the king, peace be upon him, warned us (Psalms 32:9), "be not like a horse or a mule without understanding" etc. And it is explained there, in portion Kedoshim (80a), at the beginning of the explanation of this verse, regarding the matter of union — these are his words: fortunate are the righteous who occupy themselves with Torah and know the ways of the Holy One, blessed be He, and sanctify themselves with the holiness of the King, and are found holy in everything; therefore they draw a spirit of holiness from above, and their children are all truly righteous, and are called sons of the King, holy children. Woe to the wicked, whose whole selves are brazen and whose deeds are brazen — therefore their children inherit a brazen soul from the impure side, and just as it is written (Leviticus 11:43), "and you become defiled by them" — he comes to be defiled and is defiled. "Be not like a horse or a mule" — these are the masters of lustfulness over everything. "Without understanding" — that people should not occupy themselves in this way, for if so, here it says "without understanding," and there it is written (Isaiah 56:11), "and the dogs are greedy of soul, they know not satiety, and they are shepherds who know not understanding" — meaning, behold those who are called "greedy of soul" are found among them. Why? Because "they know not understanding." "And they are shepherds" — what are shepherds? These are ones who lead and drive a person to Gehinnom. "They know not satiety" — as it is said (Proverbs 30:15), "the leech has two daughters, 'Give, give'" — therefore, being "give, give," they know not satiety. "They all turn to their own way, each to his gain from every quarter" — for these are the wanderers of Gehinnom. And what causes all this? Because they did not sanctify themselves in that union as required. Therefore it is written (Leviticus 19:2), "you shall be holy, for I am holy." The Holy One, blessed be He, said, of all the other nations, My desire was not to attach Myself except to Israel, as it is written (Deuteronomy 4:4), "and you who cling to the LORD" — you, and not the other nations, worshippers of idols. Therefore it is written here, "holy"; therefore, "you shall be holy, for I, the LORD, am holy" — precisely "you shall be [holy]." Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:15: Behold, this is the punishment of one who does not sanctify himself, and the essence of holiness depends on a person being occupied with Torah and attached to it properly, so that he not come to think of lustfulness — this is what they said at the beginning of the statement, "fortunate are those who occupy themselves with Torah." And it is further explained there, before this, regarding the punishment of the unlearned who do not occupy themselves with Torah, that they draw for their children a soul that is not holy, since Torah guides a person and teaches him how to sanctify himself.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:16: And what is said at the end of the statement, "you shall be holy, precisely," it seems to me that the intent is to be precise about the word "tihyu" [you shall be], the intent being the language of "being," alluding to the coming-into-being of souls, that they be in holiness — for otherwise it would say "and you shall sanctify yourselves," as it said previously in the portion.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:17: And should you say, if a person sanctifies his thought and removes it from thinking of physicality, he would never come to arousal at all — how then is it possible for there to be union of souls now in our time, with it being in holiness, since these two seem contradictory? One may answer that we learn the manner of a person's sanctification from Rashbi, peace be upon him, in several places. One is in the Ra'aya Meheimna (portion Tzav, beginning of 34), these are his words: and the offering of letters — yod in "ish" [man/husband], heh in "ishah" [woman/wife], vav in the son, the bridegroom, heh in the bride — fortunate is one who brings near the letters of YHVH within himself, his wife, his son, and his daughter, in holiness, in blessing, in cleanliness, in humility, and in shamefacedness, and in all the good qualities written concerning the masters of the Mishnah, and who becomes warmed by the holy fires of "ish" and "ishah" [man and woman] — which are fires that rise and fires that descend, the holiness of the wood of the arrangement, which are the holy trees, holy limbs; and the fire from on high descends, which is the Holy of Holies. And regarding these two fires the prophet said (Isaiah 24:15), "therefore glorify the LORD in the fires [urim]" — for these are the fires of the great Shechinah, "for the LORD your God is a consuming fire" (Deuteronomy 4:24). And these — the supernal fire is the throne of mercy, the lower fire is the throne of judgment, namely Binah and Malchut; Malchut is a rising fire, Binah is a descending fire; YHVH, the middle pillar, holds both of them — Binah [is] YHVH, Malchut, Tiferet, when it holds them, Chochmah rests upon it, which contains KaCh MaH [the numerical values], namely Yod-Kei and Vav-Kei; its power [koach] is Yod-Vav-Dalet Heh-Aleph Vav-Aleph-Vav Heh-Aleph, and all these are the 42 letters found in a man and his wife and their children; therefore no person is complete except with a son and a daughter — one who has no son, who is the vav, has the yod removed; and one who has no daughter has no heh, who is the daughter, [and] the supernal heh, which is the mother of his mate, is removed, for the letters do not rest, one without the other. Therefore, with a man and a woman, a son and a daughter, when properly made, YHVH rests upon them, and they are called children of the Holy One, blessed be He — this is what is written (Deuteronomy 14:1), "you are children to the LORD your God." Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:18: What is relevant to our subject is the matter of "and they become warmed by the holy fires of man and woman," as explained in Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer, that between man and woman the Name Yah is placed; and when man and woman conduct themselves properly, the Shechinah is between them, but if not, God forbid, the Name Yah departs and there remain fire and fire, and fire "consumes to destruction" (Job 31:12). Now, the fire that is in the man is sweetened more than the judgment of the woman, for in the man the yod is placed between the aleph and the shin, whereas in "ishah" [woman] the heh is at the end; and the secret of this is that "ish" [man] is a descending fire, "ishah" [woman] is a rising fire. And it is known that every descent is the flow that descends in descent, for everything that descends does so swiftly, by a direct path, to bestow; while the female is returning light, and is called "ishah," a rising fire — meaning it rises in order to receive. And he must intend that his limbs become warmed through the supernal fire, which is the Holy of Holies flowing from Binah, which is the Holy of Holies, and likewise becomes warmed through the rising fire from the Shechinah, from the fire that is in his wife. And as is said in the statement, "YHVH, the middle pillar, holds both of them" — and his saying "holds" indicates that it grasps both of the aforementioned fires, namely as he says, "therefore glorify the LORD in the fires" — so he becomes warmed with holy fire for the sake of the mitzvah, the holiness of union. And there is a further secret of fire: the secret of the Name Elohim, which equals "esh" [fire] in its full spelling, and "hakisei" [the throne] equals Elohim [in gematria].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:19: My teacher, peace be upon him, explained regarding "becoming warmed by holy fires," that this means to guard against becoming warmed by a foreign, unpleasant fire, as explained in the Zohar (portion Acharei Mot, 77a), these are his words: and sometimes Na'amah goes out into the world to become warmed by people, and a person is found in a bond of desire with her, and he awakens from his sleep and grasps his wife and lies with her, and his intent is in that desire he had in his dream — then that person, the child he begets, comes from the side of Na'amah, for it was found in his desire, when Lilith went out and saw him and knew the matter and became attached to him, etc. He says there that that person is harmed every month. Fortunate are the righteous who sanctify themselves with the holiness of the King — of them it is written (Isaiah 66:23), "and it shall be, from new moon to new moon" [with a play on "chodesh" meaning both "month" and "newness"]. Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:20: One must intend that the evil inclination aroused for union is from the side of Gevurah, which is holy fire, as explained in the Zohar (portion Bereshit, beginning of 49), on the verse (Genesis 2:7), "and the LORD God formed [vayitzer] man" — these are his words: "and the LORD God formed man" is spelled with a double yod, including both the good inclination and the evil inclination. Why? The good inclination is for himself; the evil inclination is to be aroused toward the female, and from the left side there is continual arousal toward the female. The secret of the matter: from here we learn that the north is continually aroused toward the female and becomes bound with her, and therefore she is called "ishah" [woman]. Come and see: the good inclination and the evil inclination — because the female is placed between them and bound with them, she is not bound until the evil inclination is aroused toward her and they become bound one with the other; and once they are bound one with the other, then the good inclination, which is joy, is aroused and brings her toward him. And above, the side of north itself, which is joy without the filth of the evil inclination, grasps her first, as it is written (Song of Songs 2:6), "his left hand is under my head," and afterward "and his right hand embraces me" — and then she is placed between them to be corrected. Therefore "and the LORD God formed" is written with the full Name, corresponding to these two sides, the good inclination and the evil inclination; "man" — we have established this; but male and female are not separated so as to be face to face [i.e., they are one until separated]. Thus far his words. It is thus explained that above, Gevurah, which is the left, from which the evil inclination is drawn, is what arouses union; and the intent of what we explained above is that in Atzilut there is no evil inclination, God forbid — this is what is meant by "without the filth of the evil inclination," for it is in the continuation of judgment downward, in the external forces, that the evil inclination becomes filth, namely that his inclination desires pleasure and the like; but above it is only joy that is aroused from the left, and it is the spiritual fire in the secret of the Name Elohim, as is said, that the good inclination and the evil inclination were created in the full Name YHVH Elohim — namely, YHVH is the good inclination, to guide the male, which are the acts of kindness, and the evil inclination is Elohim, which are the acts of severity, to guide the female, who is "ishah," "fire of Heh"; and this is [the meaning of] "man," which is the union of male and female face to face, the union of Chesed and Din, YHVH Elohim. Behold, when a person thinks of the aspect of the inclination to arouse it for the sake of holiness, the inclination itself becomes sanctified and resembles its supernal root.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:21: It seems to me that if arousal comes to a person that he did not intend for the sake of a mitzvah, he should dig his fingernails into the ground, and likewise meditate on the day of death, until his desire subsides; and afterward, at the time of union, he should return and arouse himself for the sake of holiness, in the manner described, by thinking of the holy Names mentioned — and in this way he guards the drop from the evil inclination, as is explained in Tikkunim (Tikkun 17, 27a), these are his words: and in like manner, in a person's union, he must purify the drop from sin, which is the evil inclination, so that the seed be pure through the letter heh — this is what is written (Genesis 47:23), "behold, seed for you." Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:22: Nevertheless, since it is impossible for a person to be entirely free of the evil inclination on account of his being clothed in matter after the sin of Adam, and matter necessarily has some pleasure even when he intends everything properly — for this reason a person becomes impure through the emission of the drop, since the evil inclination is clothed within him in any case.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:23: Regarding the holiness of union and its intent, they explained in Tikkunim (25a) that it resembles the unification a person performs in the Amidah prayer, and it says there that just as when a person prays the Amidah it is done quietly, so union must be done quietly. These are his words: at the time they are in a single union, Israel must stand in prayer quietly, and the secret of the matter — they bring her [the Shechinah] quietly; therefore, when Israel stand in the Amidah to arouse toward her the eighteen blessings quietly, to pour blessings upon her — it is said of the Chayot (Ezekiel 1:24), "when they stood, they let down their wings" — meaning that no voice need be heard, like Chanah of whom it is said (1 Samuel 1:13), "and her voice was not heard." Likewise Israel must unite with their mates quietly, in humility, in trembling and awe, and covered — as the early ones established: like one overcome by a demon [shed], which is from Shaddai [one of God's Names], for at that time he is removed from the gate — and this is the secret of the mezuzah, of which it is said (Deuteronomy 6:9), "and you shall write them on the doorposts [mezuzot] of your house" — "mezuzot" is spelled [as an acronym for] "hazemot" [lewd thoughts]; and if his voice is heard, immediately "sin crouches at the door" (Genesis 4:7), and moreover he is small in faith — and it was not for nothing that the early ones established, whoever raises his voice in his prayer is among the lesser in faith. Thus far his words, regarding union.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:24: Further there: at the time they unite, "let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth" — what is "the kisses of his mouth"? Two lips of his and two of hers, these being the four wings of the Chayot spoken of (Ezekiel 1:6), "and each had four wings" — and when his two faces and her two are joined together, and the four arms of the two of them, of them it is said (ibid.), "and each had four faces, and each of the four had four wings" — and these are the four faces YHVH, the four wings Adonai, in a single joining, YAHDONHAI. Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:25: And what is said, to unite with his mate in trembling, awe, and covering, is likewise found in the Zohar (portion Va'etchanan, 269a), these are his words: "and when you lie down" — to conduct himself in fear of his Master, in holiness, in humility, so that he not be found brazen before his Master. Thus far his words. And certainly one who has relations without covering is brazenness; and so they said in the Gemara (Niddah 16b, see Tosafot s.v. "u'mashtin"), there are three whom the Holy One, blessed be He, hates, and one of them is one who has relations naked. Nevertheless, this does not mean to say that he should have relations while [fully] dressed, for they said (Ketubot 48a), if he in his clothing and she in her clothing, he must divorce her and pay her ketubah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:26: Rashbi explained in Tikkunim (Tikkun 58, 92a), these are his words: and at that time, when they remove these garments, they unite with her husband in closeness of flesh; this is what is written (Genesis 2:23), "bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh; this one shall be called Woman, for from Man was she taken. Therefore a man shall leave his father and his mother and cleave to his wife, and they shall become one flesh" — for so it is the way of male and female to unite in closeness of flesh, and this is the clinging of the supernal union, that nothing should intervene; and therefore the masters of the Mishnah established that a person who prays unites the Holy One, blessed be He, with His Shechinah, that nothing intervene between him and the wall, without separation or division between the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah. And the secret of the matter (ibid. 2:25), "and the two of them were naked, the man and his wife" — naked, in closeness of flesh without any garment at all. Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:27: Let us return to the statement from portion Kedoshim that we copied above, and explain in it some matter according to the plain meaning, for in this statement the intent of union is explained — what it should be. He said, "therefore a person must gladden his wife at that time" — one of the good intentions that Ra'avad, peace be upon him, wrote in Sha'ar HaKedushah, as Rabbeinu Yaakov, the author of the Tur, copied in Tur Orach Chaim (§240), is that he should intend to fulfill the mitzvah of onah [conjugal duty], which is a positive commandment (Exodus 21:10), "and her conjugal rights he shall not diminish" — and this is what is meant by "a person must gladden his wife, to invite her with a single desire together with him" — meaning that her will should be attached to his, that there be no accusation or discord between them, but rather love, brotherhood, peace, and companionship, especially on Shabbat. And so it is explained in Tikkunim (57a), that one should say to her words of appeasement; and so it is explained in portion Bereshit (Zohar, portion Bereshit, 49b), these are his words: from here we learn that whoever unites with his wife must appease her and sweeten her with words, and if not, he should not sleep with her, so that their desire be as one, without coercion, etc.; and he explained there [that these are] words of love: "this time, bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh, this one shall be called Woman"; see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:28: "And both should intend as one for that matter" — meaning that he must tell her to direct her mind toward holiness, to draw down a holy soul with the union, to beget in soul and in body, so that they resemble the supernal reality — for just as Ze'ir [Anpin] and his mate attach themselves in their inwardness and outwardness as one, so below they must resemble their root; this is what is meant by "one soul and one body." It appears from the wording that one must intend that just as the body of a person is completed from its deficiency, namely the rib that was taken from man when he unites, so too his soul is likewise deficient, since souls too, when emanated from above, are emanated male and female, as explained in the Zohar (portion Lech Lecha, 91b), regarding "the daughter of so-and-so for so-and-so," and below they are separated; thus in union, the souls, male with female, are completed, and likewise in the existence of their bodies, as explained — this is "one soul and one body," that just as there is unity in the body, so in the soul. This premise is necessary and true beyond any doubt, and there is no place here to elaborate.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:29: "Then the Holy One, blessed be He, rests upon the 'one' and brings forth a holy spirit" — the matter is that just as, in the supernal reality, the Infinite, blessed and exalted be He, does not rest His unity upon a blemished throne, but only when it is entirely unified as one do they shine with the supernal light, so in the lower reality, when they [husband and wife] unite themselves with the intent described, they merit having a holy soul; this is what is meant by "a spirit of holiness."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:30: "Fortunate are those who have established this matter on none but Him alone" — this is the secret of the supernal Atzilut, namely "ANI [I] HaShem [the LORD]," and not in the lower worlds. And he said, "therefore, you shall be holy, for I, the LORD your God, am holy" — these are the secret of Nefesh, Ruach, Neshamah that come into being from the supernal union, and this suffices for the one who understands.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:31: And it is likewise fitting to intend what Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Zohar, portion Bereshit, 12b), the sixth commandment, to occupy oneself with procreation — whoever occupies himself with procreation causes that river [Yesod] to flow continually, its waters never ceasing, and the sea [Malchut] is completed on all sides, and new souls are continually renewed and issue from that tree, and great hosts increase above together with those souls. Thus far his words, as relevant to our purpose.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:32: Among the requirements of the holiness of union is that the union be face to face and not face against back, as explained in the Zohar (portion Pekudei, 259a), these are his words: here is the union and bond as one, that above and below become one in bonding, so that no limb of one is separated from the other, and all are found face to face; and therefore we have learned that whoever has relations with his bed [i.e., his wife] from behind weakens the arrangement of the gazing face to face, which illuminates all as one, and [prevents] the finding of face to face in proper attachment, as it is said (Genesis 2:24), "and he shall cleave to his wife" — precisely "to his wife," and not "behind his wife." Thus far his words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:33: The matter of "behind his wife" is the "overturning of the table" spoken of in tractate Nedarim (20a): why are children born lame? Because [their parents] overturn their table. And Rashi, peace be upon him, explained that they overturn faces toward the back, coming upon their wives unnaturally [i.e., anally]; and so wrote the Rosh, that it is because they overturn their table to have relations unnaturally, and measure for measure, because he burdens her on her knees, therefore the children are lame-footed. Thus far his words. And everything found afterward in the Gemara regarding the overturning of the table that was permitted in the Gemara, where it says (ibid. 20b) that a certain woman came before Rav and said to him, "I set the table for him and he overturned it" — and he said, how does this differ from a fritter [i.e., turning over normally in the natural manner]? This is certainly its correct meaning. I have written this to exclude those who cast off from themselves awe and shame and emit their seed in vain, who have relations in the impure orifice, the place of excretion, since intercourse there cannot produce offspring — and they already said, why are children born lame? Because they overturn their table. And Rambam, peace be upon him, wrote in chapter 21 of Hilchot Issurei Bi'ah (halakhah 9) that he should not emit seed in vain — and if intercourse is performed there, it is indeed in vain. And so it appears from the words of Ra'avad, peace be upon him, in Sha'ar HaKedushah, that the intent of the aforementioned "overturning of the table" is nothing but face against back, and its matter concerns procreation, as explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:34: I found that my teacher, peace be upon him, wrote of ways by which a person may sanctify himself, and among them he explained something of the holiness of marital relations, and we shall copy his words here. These are his words: a person rides upon the external [forces] in a way, and there are several aspects to it that require cunning to be saved from it; the main point, on which everything depends, is that the foundation of every single thing should have no grasp at all — as in the saying (Jeremiah 22:13), "woe to him who builds his house without righteousness [tzedek]" — and "tzedek" is Malchut. This means one whose every deed is for the sake of Heaven, the secret of unification: "shem" [name] there means Malchut, "shamayim" [heaven] means Tiferet, and when a person places the Name of Heaven first in all his deeds, immediately the kelipah is removed from there; but if his deeds are not for the sake of Heaven, immediately the evil [force] leaps there and rules over that matter. Therefore a person's deeds must be for the sake of Heaven: in thought, that he direct his thought in that act toward the unification of his Maker, as is known; in speech, that he mention with his mouth the unification of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah; and in deed, that the deed not be flawed — for thought and speech will not help if the vessel itself is unseemly and does not rest properly. Therefore, when building a house [i.e., a family], let his thought be for the service of his Maker, his speech for the sake of Heaven — the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah — and his deed [likewise]; and then righteousness [tzedek] will lodge in that matter and the evil [force] will be separated from there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:35: This is a great principle in procreation, in the union of a man and his wife — for there is nothing that the wicked Lilith is more eager to be present at than this very act, since it is a great building, either to beget a viable child who builds the world, or to beget children for terror in the name of Lilith, as explained in the Sava (portion Mishpatim, 96a-b) regarding "the oppressed," or to beget wicked ones, children of Samael and Lilith, destroyers of the world.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:36: This matter is therefore very difficult, and requires great preparations and precautions to escape her. The first preparation is the purification of a person from his sins as much as possible, through repentance before his Maker. The second preparation is to guard himself from sin while she is a niddah [menstrually impure], for then she is partnered [with the impure force], and if he sins with her afterward it attaches itself to her offspring. The third preparation is the proper purification of the woman according to law, and the cutting of her fingernails — the twenty that grew during her niddah — which cause harm to the world, and likewise some of her hair, as is explained at the end of portion Acharei Mot (79a) and also in the Zohar (portion Pinchas, end of 248): he should bury them in her courtyard in a designated, known spot, and when she comes to immerse he should burn them, since that part belongs to the external forces as their portion of her impurity and requires disposal, and there is no disposal except by burning. The fourth preparation is his union with her in holiness, with intent of heart, and discreetly. In the Zohar, portion Vayikra (19a), a particular incantation is explained, to be said at the time of union in order to distance this wickedness from him; and it is already explained in the Bar Metzora [a text] the sign of the holy way that he should sanctify himself at the time of relations, and the essential thing overall is not by the light of a candle and with covering, and also that he wash his hands after midnight before union in order to remove the spirit of impurity.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:37: In this manner a person should distance himself from all things that cause blemish to the soul, for she [the impure force] has an entry point through all of them, and he should distance himself from all filthy things and from all places where harmful forces are found, for all of these will cause him harm — and likewise from houses of idolatry, such as their houses of worship, their courthouses, their places of assembly, to distance himself from a harlot by four cubits, and not to gaze in his mind upon their lewdness and the like, for these things cause harm to a person, and immediately the woman of harlotry pursues him to make him lustful even in what is permitted to him, and the like among evil things, apart from several other things such as all kinds of sorcery and divination and gazing at them, since a person is exposed to chance encounters with them, as they are readily available to a person at any moment, and this is their joy, to attach themselves to him. Above all, he should be careful not to be a man of strife and quarrel within his household, for this is her main foothold, since she is immediately found there. And when he knows that he corresponds to the supernal bridegroom and she to the supernal bride, and by causing strife he drives peace from between the two, immediately the wickedness takes hold there — there is no doubt that a person will see that this is a great blemish. And strife in the house of a woman in labor causes danger to the child, and immediately she [the wicked force] is found there. And strife in a place of joy, such as [the house of] a bridegroom and bride, God forbid, causes great harm and attaches itself to that house, as in the matter of (Jeremiah 22:13), "woe to him who builds his house without righteousness."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:38: Likewise he should beware of disgusting things which she grasps onto, and of eating them in filthy places, for it was not for nothing that it is explained (Makkot 16b) [regarding] "do not make your souls detestable" (Leviticus 11:43) — this refers to one who drinks from the cupping-horn of a bloodletter — for all these things cause the soul to become detestable through this wickedness, whose dwelling is in filth. Likewise he should be careful not to be filthy in his hands or unclean in his garments, and our Sages of blessed memory have already warned Torah scholars about this, explaining the reason (Shabbat 114a): "all who hate me love death" (Proverbs 8:36) — certainly this is death without doubt. And he should not eat carelessly, by chance, without intent, sitting for the honor of his Maker, since she too presents herself by chance. And he should not bless with soiled and filthy hands, and the like — our Sages of blessed memory have already elaborated on this — all these are negative commandments.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:39: And there are positive commandments, such as being careful about Havdalah after he has blessed, to pray until they [the harmful forces] are separated from him, since that is when they grow stronger, and one should lengthen the verses of protection according to his ability. Likewise, when he goes out of the doorway of his house, and especially at night, and the protection of his Maker is at the doorway, and he goes out and is separated from it, and the external [force] is to his left, he should pray there to his Maker that his protection be with him on his way — this is (Psalms 85:14), "righteousness [tzedek] shall walk before Him," namely the attribute of Tzedek.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:40: Likewise in his actions, such as in washing his hands, to give precedence to the right over the left, as explained in the Zohar (portion Miketz, 198b), and likewise every time, he should not give precedence to the left foot over the right, nor the left hand over the right hand, but rather the reverse — the right hand over the left, the right foot over the left, always, and with intent to subdue the external [force].
